map.goal: I want to make easy small talk with colleagues over dinner on a business trip
map.title: Spanish Small Talk for Business Dinners
map.summary: To make easy small talk with colleagues at dinner, you'll need to handle introductions, polite conversation starters, sharing about yourself, and responding naturally. This map starts with greetings and introductions, then builds the grammar, vocabulary, and listening skills needed for confident, fr

sectors.title: Dinner Conversation Situations
sectors.description: Typical moments you’ll face at a business dinner, from greetings to chatting about food and work.

sectors.title: Key Expressions and Grammar
sectors.description: Useful phrases and structures for polite, friendly, and natural small talk.

sectors.title: Essential Vocabulary
sectors.description: Words and word families you’ll need for dinner, work, and casual conversation.

sectors.title: Pronunciation and Listening
sectors.description: How Spanish small talk sounds and how to follow it at a natural pace.

topics.title: Greeting and Introducing Yourself
topics.summary: You'll be able to greet colleagues and introduce yourself confidently at the dinner table.

activities.task: Practise introducing yourself and greeting a colleague.
Watch real greetings and introductions.
activities.listenFor: ¿Cómo te llamas? | Mucho gusto | Encantado de conocerte

links.why: The basic introduction structures in B1 are what you use when greeting in A1.
Hearing natural greetings in D1 prepares you for real conversations in A1.

topics.title: Basic Introduction Structures
topics.summary: You'll be able to use set phrases for introducing yourself and others.

activities.task: Practise building and swapping introduction sentences.
activities.starter: Me llamo Marta y trabajo en ventas.

activities.task: Review key introduction phrases and connectors.

links.why: You use these introduction sentences when greeting in A1.

topics.title: Starting Small Talk at the Table
topics.summary: You'll be able to open a friendly conversation and ask simple questions at dinner.

activities.task: Practise starting a casual conversation with a colleague.
activities.starter: ¿Es tu primera vez en esta ciudad?

activities.task: Roleplay starting small talk with a new colleague at dinner.

links.why: The question forms and polite openers in B2 are what you use to start conversations in A2.
The vocabulary for cities and travel in C1 helps you ask and answer about the location in A2.

topics.title: Polite Questions and Small Talk Openers
topics.summary: You'll be able to ask about travel, dinner, and the city in a friendly, polite way.

activities.task: Practise polite question forms for small talk.
Watch how people ask polite questions in conversation.

links.why: These polite openers help you start conversations in A2.
Hearing polite questions in D2 helps you recognise them in real time.

topics.title: Dinner and City Vocabulary
topics.summary: You'll know the words for typical foods, drinks, and places in the city.

activities.task: Review and test yourself on dinner and city words.
Watch for food and city words in context.
activities.listenFor: la cena | el centro | un restaurante

links.why: You use these words when chatting about dinner and the city in A2.

topics.title: Talking About Work and Roles
topics.summary: You'll be able to ask and answer about jobs and what people do at work.

activities.task: Practise asking and answering about your job.
Roleplay a dinner conversation about your work with a colleague.

links.why: The job and company vocabulary in C2 lets you talk about your role in A3.
The structures for describing your work in B3 are needed for A3.

topics.title: Describing Your Work and Hobbies
topics.summary: You'll be able to talk about your job and what you enjoy outside of work.

activities.task: Practise describing your work and hobbies.
activities.starter: Trabajo en marketing y me gusta correr.

activities.task: Review verbs and phrases for describing activities.

links.why: You use these structures when talking about your job in A3.
The job and hobby vocabulary in C2 supports your sentences in B3.

topics.title: Jobs and Company Vocabulary
topics.summary: You'll know the words for job titles, departments, and common business terms.

activities.task: Review job and company words.
Watch for job-related words in conversation.

links.why: These words let you talk about your work in A3.
You use this vocabulary in the sentences you build in B3.

topics.title: Hearing Greetings and Introductions
topics.summary: You'll be able to recognise and respond to greetings and introductions at natural speed.

activities.task: Watch and listen for natural greetings and introductions.
Roleplay hearing and responding to a greeting at dinner.

links.why: Listening to real greetings helps you respond quickly in A1.

topics.title: Listening for Small Talk Questions
topics.summary: You'll be able to catch and understand small talk questions in real conversations.

activities.task: Watch for small talk questions in real dinner scenes.
Roleplay responding to a small talk question at dinner.

links.why: Recognising these questions helps you join in small talk in A2.
Hearing the question forms from B2 prepares you to use and respond to them.
